title: Bonded membrane particles wrap particle-life cores in closed rings that persist, where the no-bond twin's rings vanish
summary: bondcell = sporecell3-det plus harmonic chain bonds between membrane particles M (<= 2 per particle, k_b=20, break above 0.6), bonded M kept as membrane when food is scarce, and a monolayer rule (a core particle touching >= 4 M stays core); k_cat 0.03. From a random particle soup, by t=40-70 the larger cores are dense discs fully enclosed by a closed ring of bonded M (bonded_vs_nobond.png left: 6 ringed cores at t=70, M ~320 with ~96% bonded), while the matched no-bond twin (same seed, same random streams, bonds=0) has bare cores and only 11-15 M particles from t=60 (middle, right panel). Not yet a claim: one seed to t=70, cores grow until they hold ~60% of the matter and the run slows (13-15 sub-steps per step), division and starvation survival are untested.
